parsed.main_gap: False graph claim: a multigraph with q vertices and q-1 edges need not be acyclic, and the chosen component (the one containing a_q) need not be a tree. Fix (some component is a tree) is one line but is not given.

errors.description: In the lower-bound half of the refinement lemma, the write-up asserts that fewer edges than vertices forces the whole graph to be acyclic and every component to be a tree. This is false (e.g. a triangle plus an isolated vertex). Moreover it bipartitions the component containing a_q, which may contain a cycle/loop and hence admit no valid bipartition. Repairable by noting that q vertices with ≤ q−1 edges forces at least one tree component, and using that one.
errors.quote:
Having fewer edges than vertices, the graph contains
no cycle and no loop, since a cycle or a loop on \(v\) vertices already uses at
least \(v\) edges; hence every connected component \(C\) has \(e_C=v_C-1\) and
is a tree (an isolated vertex counts as a tree). We use the component
containing the vertex of \(a_q\).

errors.description: The 56-unit 'grid example' is presented as agreeing with the theorem, but Liu's marks (7,21) give initial lengths 7,14,35 with Γ = 7/56 = 1/8, not 1/7; the displayed outcome 4/7 arises only because Xiang played suboptimally. Labeled as evidence, so harmless, but the claim of 'agreement with the theorem' is misleading.
errors.quote:
Liu marks \((7,21)\), Xiang marks \((8,38)\), and the physical lengths are
\((7,1,13,17,18)\). Sorting gives Liu
\((18+13+1)/56=32/56=4/7\), in agreement with the theorem.

parsed.notes: Answer 2^n/(2^{n+1}-1) with a correct greedy-drafting lemma, a correct subset-sum pigeonhole upper bound, and a correct overlay construction. Only the acyclicity step in the key lower-bound lemma is wrong, and it is trivially patchable.
